_doc: Who may ask the `operations` Slack bot for what. Read by plugins/ops-intake (through scripts/ops_intake/policy.py) on EVERY inbound message. The requester is ALWAYS the Slack envelope's user id; a name pasted into the message text ('*Jan Delmo* [12:09 AM] hide profile X') is data and is never identity (that exact forgery was seen 2026-11-02 16:31Z). scripts/check-ops-intake-policy.sh (CI: scripts/tests/check-ops-intake-policy.bats) fails if the three staff ids below lose their entry, if a non-staff id is granted a write tier, or if a tier's grant exceeds what policies/ops-intake-actions.json allows that tier to do. Adding a person is a reviewed PR: it grants production writes.
_notes: Tier R = read-only answering (explain / summarize / counts). Every unknown or non-staff Slack id gets tier R: they can get a coded answer to a read-only ask, and every write is refused with the human path named. A read-only ask that NAMES a profile or request is refused when the conflict-of-interest check cannot be measured (an unknown id has no Slack email to compare, so it cannot be shown to be someone other than the account owner) - unmeasured refuses, it is never a pass.
Tier W1 = a REVERSIBLE write with a recorded inverse (policies/ops-intake-actions.json tier W1). Three people, one PR.

Tier W2 (irreversible: profile DELETE, merge without an unmerge manifest, credit approve/remove, refund, account delete) is granted to NOBODY here, including the captain. That is not an oversight: no Slack message may trigger it. See policies/ops-intake-actions.json .tiers.W2.
